advisory.finding: The new scan accepts ANY `encoding` keyword, whatever its value. The old guard required the literal "utf-8". So `encoding=None`, which means the locale codec (cp1252 on Windows), or any non-UTF-8 codec now passes, although the test claims to enforce UTF-8.
merged_from: The scan misses text mode passed through a keyword splat from a dict *literal*. Neither arm fires: `**` keywords have `kw.arg is None` and are dropped, and a `{...}` literal is not an `ast.Call`. A regression written in that style passes the guard.
scenarios: A later edit writes `encoding=None` or `encoding=locale.getpreferredencoding()` on a git call, and the Windows mojibake bug comes back with the guard still green
The 5 CLI-consumer modules the old guard pinned to utf-8 could now switch to another codec without any test failing
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `if "encoding" in kwargs or mode is None: continue` with: `enc = kwargs.get("encoding"); if mode is None or (isinstance(enc, ast.Constant) and enc.value == "utf-8"): continue`. Add the cases `('subprocess.run(["git"], text=True, encoding=None)', True)` and `('subprocess.run(["git"], text=True, encoding="cp1252")', True)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add errors="replace" (or catch UnicodeDecodeError) on the `git grep` call in sunset_markers.py so non-UTF-8 source lines don't crash the scan
evidence: ["git", "-C", code_root, "grep", "-n", "--fixed-strings", "--", MARKER], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", check=False,
`except OSError as exc:` immediately follows the call; UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError subclass, not an OSError.
`git grep -n` emits the matching file lines verbatim, so bytes come from repository file content, not from git's own UTF-8 metadata.
Contrast: _bridge_runner.py, grounding/harness.py and acli_subprocess.py pair encoding="utf-8" with errors="replace"; this call does not.
advisory.finding: The `git grep` call in sunset_markers.py now strictly decodes matched source lines as UTF-8 with no `errors=` policy. Its handler only catches OSError, so a match inside a non-UTF-8 file raises an uncaught UnicodeDecodeError.
scenarios: A repo containing a Latin-1 or Shift-JIS source file that contains MARKER on a line with non-ASCII bytes.
On Windows the previous cp1252 decode almost never failed. With strict UTF-8 it now crashes the sunset-markers command.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `errors="replace"` alongside `encoding="utf-8"` in the `git grep` subprocess.run call in sunset_markers.py.

evidence: ["git", "-C", str(checkout), "show", f"HEAD:{path}"], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", check=False,  # a path absent at HEAD is counted, not fatal
`git show HEAD:<path>` emits the blob's raw bytes, which are not guaranteed to be UTF-8.

advisory.finding: engine_comparison.py reads file contents via `git show HEAD:{path}` and decodes them strictly as UTF-8. A non-UTF-8 file at HEAD raises UnicodeDecodeError instead of being counted like an absent path.
scenarios: Eval checkout containing a Latin-1-encoded fixture, or a binary file at one of the compared paths.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `errors="replace"` to the `git show HEAD:{path}` subprocess.run call in engine_comparison.py.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the encoding scan reject `encoding=None` and flag `subprocess.getoutput`/`getstatusoutput` calls
evidence: _SUBPROCESS_RUNNERS = frozenset({"run", "Popen", "check_output", "check_call", "call"})

if "encoding" in kwargs or mode is None:
            continue
Absence: `getoutput`/`getstatusoutput` are not in _SUBPROCESS_RUNNERS, and the rule requires a text/universal_newlines keyword, which those APIs never take.
advisory.finding: The new tree-wide guard does not catch every locale-codec decode path. It treats any `encoding` keyword as compliant, including `encoding=None`, which falls back to the locale codec. It also omits `subprocess.getoutput`/`getstatusoutput`, which always decode with the locale codec and take no text/encoding keyword.
scenarios: A future `subprocess.run(..., text=True, encoding=None)` passes the guard yet decodes as cp1252 on Windows.
A future `subprocess.getoutput("git ...")` reintroduces cp1252 decoding undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _locale_decoded_text_calls, only treat the call as compliant when `encoding` is a non-None value: `enc = kwargs.get("encoding"); if enc is not None and not (isinstance(enc, ast.Constant) and enc.value is None): continue`. Separately, flag any `subprocess.getoutput`/`subprocess.getstatusoutput` call.

dropped.finding: The tree-wide test only checks that `offenders == []`, a list built from an rglob file walk, with no liveness anchor. If the walk scans zero files, or the scan stops recognising subprocess calls, the test still passes, so it cannot tell 'clean' from 'scanned nothing'.
scenarios: After a src-layout move or a change to REPO_ROOT resolution, rglob yields nothing and the guard stays green forever
dropped.suggested_fix: Collect `paths = sorted((REPO_ROOT / "src" / "rebar").rglob("*.py"))` and `assert paths`. Also assert that a known module such as `src/rebar/_commands/verify_commit.py` is in `paths`, so the walk is known to reach the changed tree.
